arguments.rule_content:
rule YARA_CobaltStrike_Generic {
    meta:
        description = "Detects generic Cobalt Strike beacons via entropy and strings"
        author = "SOC Team"
        false_positives = ["Packed .NET assemblies", "Signed Microsoft binaries"]
        remediation = "Exclude known Microsoft-signed binaries by certificate or hash"
    strings:
        $beacon_config = { 2E 72 63 64 2E 63 66 67 }
        $http_get = "GET / HTTP/1.1" wide
        $user_agent = "User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0" wide
    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and filesize < 2MB and
        $beacon_config and $http_get and $user_agent and
        not pe.imphash() == "f34d5f2d4577ed6d9ceec516c1f5a744" and
        not hash.sha256(0, filesize) == "a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2"
}

arguments.summary: A spear-phishing campaign attributed to APT-41 (Double Dragon) successfully compromised a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042) via malicious Outlook macro execution. The initial payload, 'chrome_helper.exe', executed a multi-stage attack involving PowerShell-based code execution, DLL sideloading via rundll32.exe, and deployment of a ShadowPad variant. The malware established C2 communication over HTTPS to a known malicious infrastructure and attempted lateral movement via SMB. Detection occurred via IDS signature for Cobalt Strike beaconing, though the initial phishing vector was not blocked. No containment actions were executed due to policy enforcement failures.

arguments.summary: A post-exploitation incident was initiated from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) after a spear-phishing compromise via Outlook. The malware sample 'taskeng_monitor.exe' (hash: e9f0a1b2...) showed limited behavior in sandbox analysis but omitted critical lateral movement and credential theft activities. The source IP 10.0.5.14 in the original alert appears to be a misattribution; all evidence points to 10.0.5.42 as the true origin.
